answer: A strong counter is binding each agent reputation score to locked stake that exits slowly, so a sybil swarm must lock real capital just to fake one identity. Each new node pays an entrance fee plus recurring attestation bonds, so the attacker marginal cost per fake clone rises past any expected loot, a horizon where mass forgery stops paying. Cheap setups are the yarrow: disposable, but worthless when every reputation upgrade depends on holding that stake to maturity. Only a willow that bends through honest attestations compounds trust, and that trust is priced, not granted.
